patient_information: A 25-year-old Malawian primary school teacher, HIV-positive, on first-line antiretroviral therapy (ART) with tenofovir, lamivudine and efavirenz for 6 months with good adherence, with a CD4 count of 320 cells/",µL on starting ART.
chief_complaint: Abrupt onset of fever and confusion.
history_of_present_illness: Well at 8 a.m., confused by 10 a.m., and drowsy with a high fever and convulsions on admission at 11 a.m.; completed treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis 2 months ago.
exposure_and_epidemiology: Malawian primary school teacher; HIV-positive; completed treatment for pulmonary tuberculosis 2 months ago.
vitals: Temperature 40"C (104"F), pulse 125 bpm, blood pressure 125/68 mmHg, oxygen saturation 93% on room air.
physical_exam: Restless and agitated; Glasgow Coma Scale 10/15; pupils equal and reactive with photophobia; neck stiff; no rash; plantar responses down-going; Kernig's sign positive; chest and abdominal examinations unremarkable; suffered a renewed seizure during the physical examination.
labs_and_diagnostics: Blood results: WBC 10.5"><10^9/L, neutrophil count 8.9"><10^9/L, haemoglobin 8.9 g/dL, MCV 85 fL, platelets 255"><10^9/L, creatinine 106 ",µmol/L, random blood glucose 5.6 mmol/L. Spinal tap results: hazy CSF, leukocytes 35 cells/",µL (60% neutrophils), protein 2.6 g/L, glucose 1.2 mmol/L. Rapid antigen test for Plasmodium falciparum negative. CSF culture grew S. pneumoniae.
differential_diagnosis: Acute bacterial meningitis (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitis, group A streptococci, Staphylococcus aureus, invasive non-typhoidal salmonellae, Salmonella typhi, Escherichia coli, Haemophilus influenzae), cryptococcal meningitis, TB meningitis, Listeria monocytogenes.
management_and_clinical_course: In the emergency department, received ceftriaxone 2g IV, diazepam 10mg IV, and phenobarbitone 600mg IV; oxygen saturation improved with resuscitation. Received 10 days of IV ceftriaxone and recovered consciousness by day 3. No further neurological impairment or seizures were noted; anticonvulsants were weaned by day 3. Audiometry revealed a minor hearing loss in her right ear.
final_diagnosis: Acute bacterial meningitis caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae.
